name: How to Use t-SNE Effectively (Distill)
oneLine: Distill's explainer on how t-SNE misleads. Serif essay prose with a live, steppable t-SNE run as the hero.

palette.note: Page ground behind both the prose and the canvas figures; no tinted panels
Deep teal-navy 70px masthead holding the Distill droplet logo and ABOUT / PRIZE / SUBMIT
Body and headings set in rgba(0,0,0,0.8), so text reads as soft charcoal instead of pure black
rgba(0,0,0,0.5) for figure metadata such as 'Perplexity: 30 / Step: 10' and secondary labels
Steel blue on the round play/pause and restart buttons and the slider thumbs; the only UI color
Faint cool tint behind small UI chips and the selected dataset-thumbnail state

type.note: Title around 56px regular with tight default tracking, sentence case; section heads ('1. Those hyperparameters really matter') around 30px regular. The old-style numerals carry the editorial tone
20px regular on about 31px leading, a measure of about 650px (65-70 characters), quotations set in true italic
12px regular for every figure label, slider caption ('Perplexity 10') and step counter; the nav is 12px uppercase with wide tracking

layout: The prose column sits about 650px wide, left-aligned at x=228 inside a 984px container. The right third stays empty beside the text, so figures can break out to the full 1080px width.

The hero puts an interactive figure right after the dek: a live point cloud on the left, a 6x3 grid of 56px dataset thumbnails on the right, and play/restart buttons, a step counter and three sliders below it.
Numbered sections are separated by full-bleed 1px hairlines with about 60px of air on each side. Small-multiple strips (one run captured at steps 10, 20, 60, 120 and 1,000) appear inline as evidence.
motion: The hero figure animates t-SNE optimization in real time. Points drift from a scrambled cloud into a structure while the 'Step' counter ticks up (87 on desktop and 74 on mobile when captured, so it runs on load).
The motion carries the meaning: watching the embedding converge is the argument, not decoration.
(inferred) Re-running with a new perplexity or epsilon restarts the animation from a random seed, so readers see run-to-run variance with their own eyes.
(inferred) Apart from the canvas animations, the page has no scroll-triggered transitions or page-level motion.
interactions: Click a dataset thumbnail (grid, clusters, rings, trefoil and others) to swap the data in the main simulation. The selected tile gets a blue outline.
Drag the sliders (Points Per Side, Perplexity, Epsilon) to re-run t-SNE live with new hyperparameters.
Play/pause and restart buttons let the reader freeze the optimization at any step.
steal: Results page hero: a live latent-space embedding of telemetry windows (normal vs. anomalous) that settles into place on load, with a visible 'epoch' or 'step' counter.
Model-comparison section: small-multiple strips of one anomaly-score plot at several thresholds or window sizes, each captioned in 12px mono ('window: 256 / thr: 0.92').
Methods section: hyperparameter sliders (window length, contamination, latent dim) that update a figure in place, so readers can see why our chosen settings matter.
leave: The 2016 masthead and stock steel-blue Material buttons feel dated and generic next to a SpaceX/Apple-level direction. Keep the idea and restyle the controls.
The all-white, serif-only presentation reads as an academic journal. Our recruiter audience needs a stronger cinematic first impression before the long-form explanation starts.
